provenance.py_hash_seed_note: The same PYTHONHASHSEED in all six colony processes, so the hash order is common-mode across colonies and cannot contaminate the between-colony comparison. The unpinned floor was measured: docs/process_noise.json.
provenance.wall_clock_note: The total elapsed time across both batches. The original single-batch run took 1,814 s with all six colonies in parallel; the re-run that carries the discovery series was split, so its total is larger than a single parallel batch even though no colony did more work.

campaign_batches.note: The six colonies were run in two batches: five in parallel, then NO_QUESTIONS alone. The first batch was interrupted before its slowest colony finished, and that colony was re-run. Every colony is an independent process with its own temporary substrate, the same seed and the same pinned PYTHONHASHSEED, so the batching is a wall-clock fact and not a scientific one. All six reproduce the original run's metrics exactly, field for field.

provenance.regenerated_note: Regenerated from the campaign's own per-colony part files so that the artifact carries the per-cycle discovery series alongside the metrics. The previously published artifact was assembled before the discovery instrumentation was added and could not produce docs/discovery.json or docs/figure_discovery.svg.

M5_development_velocity.last_100_new_rate_note: 0 means the organism discovered nothing new in the final 100 cycles. In a world that repeats, that is the repertoire being exhausted, not development slowing.

discovery.note: cumulative[k][i] is the number of DISTINCT items of kind k discovered by the end of cycle i. A curve that flattens is a repertoire being exhausted, not development slowing. m5_* counts only the four kinds M5 counts, so m5_cycle_cumulative_total ends at M5's inventory_total.
